bullets.title: Fed hikes 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, signals at least one more in 2026 — decisively hawkish
bullets.body: FOMC voted unanimously to raise the fed funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; 16 of 18 members project at least one more hike in 2026, with the median dot at 4.1% and some hawks at 4.3%. Neutral rate revised up to 3.2-3.25% (highest since 2016), core PCE forecast raised to 3.4% for 2026, and Warsh described financial conditions as 'not restrictive,' explicitly removing supply-shock language. No hikes penciled for 2027; one cut each in 2028-2029.

bullets.title: Equities sold off on hawkish Warsh presser, then partially recovered; rate-sensitive sectors hardest hit
bullets.body: S&P 500 fell as much as 1.5% intraday before closing -0.5%; NDX outperformed, closing up on the day. Banks -2.3% (Regionals -4.4%), Energy -3.0%, and Housing lagged, while Tech/Semis +0.6% and Data Center REITs +1.09%. VIX rose 0.5pts to 17.7; more stocks falling than rising for 11 of last 15 trading days with S&P A/D at -200.

bullets.title: 10Y Treasury crosses 5%; 2Y +7bp to 4.74% — JPM tactically cautious on equities into yield headwinds
bullets.body: 10-year yield hit 5.016% post-FOMC, a cycle high; 2-year +7.3bp to 4.736%. JPM notes that when 10Y makes new cycle highs, equities historically take up to 8 weeks to digest, and a 2-standard-deviation yield move correlates with negative monthly returns. Terminal rate futures imply ~4.6% fed funds (~90bp additional tightening).

bullets.title: JPM recommends long Tech/Mag7 vs. short SMid as dip-buy; Citi neutral, warns AI slowdown worsens risk/reward
bullets.body: JPM US Market Intel maintains Tactically Cautious/Neutral but recommends buying Tech/Mag7 and AI theme on dips while shorting SMid-caps. Citi stays neutral, noting equity performance hinges on 2-3 hikes then a pause plus strong EPS growth — and that any AI model development slowdown worsens the risk/reward materially.

bullets.title: Global DM central banks set for ~100bp cumulative hikes through mid-2027; financial stress risk elevated
bullets.body: JPM estimates Taylor Rule warrants ~100bp average DM tightening, with six of nine DM central banks expected to hike by end-2026 (RBA 4, ECB 3, BoJ 3, Fed 2). Crude above $100/bbl adds stagflationary pressure; JPM flags heightened risk that 100bp-scale tightening triggers a financial stress event similar to 1986-87, 1996-97, or 2013-14.

bullets.title: Gundlach exits all AI equity exposure; flags AI credit spreads widening 50-130bp, Shiller CAPE near 42
bullets.body: Gundlach cited a Shiller CAPE near 42 (every prior reading above 35 produced negative 10-year real S&P returns), with AI-linked junk bonds and loans widening 50-130bp from tights and triple-C bank loans down 5-6% in total return. He shifted 30% equity allocation to equal-weighted large-cap index and expects next CPI to 'start with a 4' given oil above $100. Warns private credit is 'the fuse' and insurance/annuity balance sheets are 'the bomb.'

bullets.title: Hedgeye nowcast: September CPI accelerates to 3.61% y/y (+21bp); inflation bias shifted to moderately inflationary
bullets.body: Hedgeye's monthly CPI nowcast (90% directional accuracy on second derivative) projects September CPI at +3.61% y/y, up 21bp from prior estimate and 7bp above the 9/11 forecast. This represents a shift from sideways to moderate inflationary bias; CPI releases October 14.

bullets.title: August import prices hotter than expected; ex-fuel +0.8% m/m vs +0.3% est, China +1.0% (record)
bullets.body: August ex-fuel import prices rose 0.8% m/m vs 0.3% expected, running at 5.5% y/y, with the broadest breadth since 2004. China import prices rose a record 1.0% m/m, the largest monthly increase since 2004, reinforcing the hawkish Fed backdrop.

bullets.title: August retail sales beat sharply: +1.4% m/m ex-auto vs +0.5% consensus; consumer resilient but gas a risk
bullets.body: August retail sales ex-auto rose 1.4% m/m vs 0.5% expected; unadjusted +6.2% y/y. CE/appliances +7.8% y/y, non-store (e-commerce) +9.9% y/y. Elevated gas prices (+21% y/y at gas stations, driven by 29.5% y/y gas price increase) pose a risk to 2H consumer spending.

bullets.title: Yardeni cuts S&P 500 year-end target 500pts to 7,900; global investors distancing from US assets
bullets.body: Ed Yardeni lowered his S&P 500 year-end target by 500 points to 7,900 citing rising economic risks. Separately, reports indicate global investors are distancing from US assets amid debt and sanctions concerns, a notable sentiment shift.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex surging to $1.4T in 2027 (+60% vs 2026's $860B); issuers going FCF-negative
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates hyperscalers issued ~$230B in bonds YTD with 2026 supply largely complete. As capex surges 60% to $1.4T in 2027, the group moves FCF-negative, with 35-40% of 2026 capex already debt-financed. Credit ETF outflows are accelerating (LQD -$1.2B/week, HYG -$640M/week), trading at widest NAV discounts since March.

bullets.title: Blackstone secures ~$22-23B in bank financing for Google AI infrastructure JV (Crux AI)
bullets.body: Blackstone lined up approximately $22-23B from 10 banks for the Crux AI joint venture with Google, which will offer data center capacity, networking, and Google Cloud TPUs as compute-as-a-service. Blackstone committed $5B in initial equity; first 500MW of capacity targeted online in 2027 with plans to scale significantly.

bullets.title: OpenAI raising at ~$1.2T valuation; Anthropic IPO moving forward — AI infrastructure capital needs accelerating
bullets.body: OpenAI is raising a private round at approximately $1.2T valuation amid ongoing capital needs, while Anthropic (which reports 80% gross margins and two quarters of adjusted operating profitability, excluding training costs and SBC) is moving forward with an IPO. The concentration of AI infrastructure capital continues to intensify.

bullets.title: GEV +4.8% on $200B backlog on track for early 2027; ~38% of electrification orders are data centers
bullets.body: GEV management confirmed the $200B order backlog target is on track for early 2027, with 2H contract commitments expected to exceed 20GW guidance. Data centers represent 38% of electrification orders; equipment backlog of $40B+ represents ~3 years of revenue. GEV is read as a bellwether for healing sentiment across the broader AI infrastructure group.

bullets.title: Tech bond issuance up $260B vs 2025, adding 10-15bp upward pressure on global yields
bullets.body: JPM estimates US tech sector net bond issuance rose ~$200B (from $140B to $335B) and ~$60B in Europe vs. 2025, implying 10-15bp upward pressure on Global Agg yields (5-10bp controlling for policy rates). Equity fund flows decelerated to near-zero in September, similar to April 2024, which proved short-lived.

bullets.title: Housing sector under pressure: homebuilder sentiment at lowest since 2022, mortgage apps -4.1% w/w, refis -65% y/y
bullets.body: US homebuilder sentiment hit its lowest level since 2022, and mortgage applications dropped 4.1% week-over-week with refinancing applications down 65% year-over-year. Higher-for-longer rates and the 25bp hike to 3.75-4% are compounding affordability pressures, with 30-year mortgage rates above 7% for the first time in 15 months.

bullets.title: WTI crude -3.2% on Saudi East-West pipeline restoration hopes; oil above $100 remains stagflationary tail risk
bullets.body: WTI crude fell 3.2% Wednesday on reports of improving Saudi East-West pipeline conditions. Despite the daily decline, crude remains above $100/bbl, which JPM and Gundlach both flag as creating a modest stagflationary impulse and a tail risk that could interrupt the global hiking cycle or force a harder Fed.

bullets.title: Stablecoins emerging as real payments infrastructure: $62T in 2025 transfers, B2B growing 65% annually
bullets.body: UBS FinovateFall recap highlights stablecoin transfers reaching ~$62T in 2025, with ~$4.2T representing real economic activity and ~$350-550B in bilateral goods/services payments. B2B stablecoin use represents ~40% of activity growing ~65% annually; key risks include de-pegging, irreversibility, and compliance uncertainty pending GENIUS Act finalization in January 2027.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk elevated: Xi-Trump summit one week away; Houthis entering Red Sea, Russia intensifying Ukraine campaign
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags a Strait of Hormuz stalemate, Houthis entering the Red Sea conflict, growing Saudi East-West pipeline threats, Russia intensifying its Ukraine campaign, and a Xi Jinping–Trump summit one week away. Congress is also taking up a Russia sanctions bill.

bullets.title: Breadth deteriorating broadly: advance/decline down 2-to-1; bond attractiveness vs. equities creating inflow headwind
bullets.body: NYSE and Nasdaq advance/decline lines running worse than 2-to-1 ratio, with more stocks falling than rising for 11 of 15 trading days. After 74 months of Treasury drawdowns, bonds are down 8.1% and now relatively attractive vs. bond proxies — creating structural headwinds for equity inflows unless growth accelerates above trend.
